<a id="structure"></a>

# Structure

Structure commands operate on nodes and block placement. The parent decides the level: a chapter under the book, a subchapter under a chapter, and a block under either.

Add a unit with `add --book <book> --title <title> --parent <node>`. Place it with `--index`, or relative to a sibling with `--before` or `--after`. The command prints the identifier of the new unit.

```text
pecia add --book guide --title "Chapter"
pecia add --book guide --title "Section" --parent <chapter>
pecia add --book guide --title "Another Chapter" --index 0
```

Link entries are added with `--link` and a cross-book reference. `--ref-book` names the target book, `--ref-node` or `--ref-block` the target unit. Links render as links and stay out of the body flow.

Move a unit with `move --child-of <node>` or relative to a sibling. A move changes the ordered collections only; the identifier and the body stay the same, and links keep working.

Rename with `rename --title`. The title is normalized and the anchor is derived from it. Because anchors change, run `sync --check` after a rename.

Remove a unit with `remove`. A chapter requires `--recursive`, which removes its subtree and its bodies. Removing a block also removes its notes and its metadata.

A block can carry a type for later search (`block type`). Locked blocks protect generated content: changing their body or type is refused, and only their owning command may update them.

Numbering is opt-in per book. Without numbering, headings use the titles and anchors are derived from them. With numbering, numbers are rendered in the heading, while anchors remain number independent.

Common structure errors are stable and descriptive: `structure.level-limit`, `structure.empty-title`, `structure.unknown-target`, `structure.anchor-mismatch` and `structure.locked`. They describe a rule, not a UI state.
